bibliographic.title: LUCE: A BLOCKCHAIN-BASED DATA SHARING PLATFORM FOR MONITORING DATA LICENSE ACCOUNTABILITY AND COMPLIANCE
bibliographic.authors: Visara Urovi; Vikas Jaiman; Arno Angerer; Michel Dumontier
bibliographic.citation_apa: Urovi, V., Jaiman, V., Angerer, A., & Dumontier, M. (2022). LUCE: A blockchain-based data sharing platform for monitoring data license accountability and compliance. arXiv preprint arXiv:2202.11646.

methodology.method_family: system architecture design with implementation and scalability evaluation
methodology.study_design: technical platform development and real-time scalability experimentation
methodology.sample_description: simulated growing number of users accessing and reusing different datasets in a real-time environment
methodology.technology_context: blockchain, smart contracts, distributed ledgers, GDPR-oriented data license monitoring

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study addresses blockchain-based data sharing accountability and license compliance, not conversational AI, LLMs, chatbots, agents, or generative AI governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper strongly addresses accountability, transparency, compliance, monitoring, traceability, and regulatory requirements (including GDPR), the provided text contains no evidence of large language models, generative AI, conversational systems, or conversational governance. Matches for interaction refer to smart-contract and data-sharing protocols, not human-machine dialogue or conversational oversight.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Clear technology mismatch with review scope; exclusion is supported by zero LLM evidence and absence of conversational AI focus in the supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects methodological quality within blockchain data-sharing research only. Transferability to LLM conversational governance is very limited based on provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The study is internally coherent for decentralized data-sharing accountability, but its relevance to conversational governance in LLM-based regulated systems is very low because the technology and application domain differ fundamentally from the review scope.

coding.theme: Decentralized accountability for regulated data sharing

synthesis.main_claim: LUCE is a decentralized blockchain-based platform that traces shared datasets and provides transparency, accountability, and legal compliance mechanisms for data reuse after third-party handoff.
synthesis.contribution: Defines a generic model and implementation for decentralized data-sharing accountability and compliance, incorporating dynamic consent and legal compliance mechanisms, with scalability testing in a real-time multi-user setting.
synthesis.limitations: Provided excerpts do not clearly document study limitations; sample size and generalizability beyond blockchain data-sharing contexts are unclear.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for LLM conversational governance; may serve only as distant contextual background on accountability/compliance infrastructure unrelated to conversational AI.
